title: for Loops and Counter-Controlled Iteration
learningObjectives: Explain initialization, condition and update in for loops.
Choose step sizes and reverse counts correctly.
Understand counter scope in the loop header.
Use for when iteration structure is known or count-driven.

understand.concept: A for header combines initialization, condition, and update. Initialization runs once; update runs after the body.
understand.whyItMatters: For loops make counter-controlled repetition and boundaries easy to see.
understand.explain: Read the header as setup → test → body → update. Verify how many values pass the condition.

practise.guidedTask: For for Loops and Counter-Controlled Iteration, trace each example in a table showing the loop's initial state, condition result, body action, update step, and final state. Identify the termination point and boundary behavior.
practise.independentTask: Write a small C++ exercise focused on for Loops and Counter-Controlled Iteration. Include at least three test cases (typical, boundary and termination/invalid-input case where relevant), trace the loop iterations, and explain why it stops or skips/continues as intended.
hints: Write down the loop's starting state.
Trace the condition before/after each pass according to loop type.
Check that every continuing path progresses toward termination.
Test boundary values and early-exit paths.
Count passes explicitly to catch off-by-one errors.

questions.prompt: What runs once before the first for test?

questions.explanation: Update follows the body and precedes next condition.
